answer.evidence: Units with |weights| well above the untrained init range (about ±69) form smooth, nodule-centred maps. Malignant-side units: 18, 8, 20, 29 and 1 have broad positive blobs over the central region (rows ~5-20, cols ~4-18). Units 2 and 27 are positive almost everywhere (overall brightness). Folding layers 2-3 together, these give the largest net positive contributions to the logit (unit 18 about +32k, unit 1 about +17.6k, unit 20 about +10.9k, unit 8 about +9.6k, unit 27 about +6k, in integer-product units). Benign-side units: 17 and 23 are surround detectors. They are positive along the image border: rows 0-6 and 21-23 for both, the right edge for 17 and the left edge for 23. Both are strongly negative in the centre (17 reaches -92 to -97 around rows 8-15; 23 reaches -76 to -85 near rows 12-15). Their net effect on the logit is only mildly benign (about -2.4k and -6k). Unit 23 is somewhat top-heavy (rows 0-4), which I considered as a possible artifact detector. However, it pairs with a strong negative centre and with the bottom and side borders, and it is weak relative to the central pathway, so it reads as centre-versus-surround contrast rather than a dedicated artifact feature. I found no compact, sharply localized patch (corner marker, text, ruler) with large weights shared by units feeding a strong dedicated pathway. The faint positive cluster near rows 15-17, cols 19-22 in units 9 and 15 stays within init-range magnitudes and looks like noise. The other units (0, 3, 16, etc.) look like random init or have drifted negative and are likely dead.
answer.main_feature: The model mainly scores the amount and extent of bright, soft-tissue-density tissue in the centre of the crop: larger, denser central nodules push toward malignant. A bright surround with a dark or small centre pushes mildly toward benign.
